word: I was sedated, but my wife, who was there, told me that when they viewed the cells under a microscope, the doctors started crying because it turned out to be a very rare form of pancreatic cancer that is curable with surgery.
meaning: 我當時被麻醉了，但在場的妻子告訴我，當他們在顯微鏡下觀察那些細胞時，醫生們開始哭泣，因為結果顯示那是一種非常罕見、可以透過手術治癒的胰腺癌。
example: While he was sedated, the doctors discovered it was a rare, curable cancer and were moved to tears.
hint:
中文解釋：命運的驚天逆轉——醫生的哭泣從壞消息變成了好消息的象徵。
1) sedated (adj.): 被麻醉的；syn: under anesthesia; ant: awake
2) curable (adj.): 可治癒的；syn: treatable; ant: incurable
pronunciation: Long: I was se-DA-ted | doc-tors START-ed CRY-ing | very RARE form | CUR-a-ble with SUR-ger-y.

word: I had the surgery, and thankfully I'm fine now.
meaning: 我接受了手術，感謝上天，我現在很好。
example: He underwent surgery and recovered successfully.
hint:
中文解釋：簡單的一句話解除了聽眾的擔憂，也帶來鬆了一口氣的情緒轉折。
1) had the surgery (phr.): 接受了手術；syn: underwent the operation; ant: declined surgery
2) thankfully (adv.): 感謝地；syn: fortunately; ant: unfortunately
pronunciation: Relief: I had the SUR-ger-y | and THANK-ful-ly | I'm FINE now.

word: This was the closest I've been to facing death, and I hope it's the closest I get for a few more decades.
meaning: 這是我離死亡最近的一次，我希望在未來幾十年裡，這就是我離死亡最近的距離了。
example: That experience was the nearest he had come to dying, and he hopes it stays that way for many years.
hint:
中文解釋：帶點幽默的希望——他從死亡邊緣回來，輕描淡寫地說「希望這是最近的距離了」。
1) the closest I've been (phr.): 我最接近的一次；syn: the nearest I got; ant: far from death
2) a few more decades (phr.): 再幾十年；syn: many more years; ant: a short time
pronunciation: Wry: the CLOS-est I've BEEN | to FA-cing DEATH | hope it's the CLOS-est I GET | for a FEW more DEC-ades.

word: Having lived through it, I can now say this to you with a bit more certainty than when death was a useful but purely intellectual concept.
meaning: 親身經歷之後，我現在可以比死亡只是一個有用卻純粹抽象的概念時，更確定地對你們說這些話。
example: After surviving this experience, he can speak about death with more personal conviction, not just theory.
hint:
中文解釋：親身經歷死亡威脅，讓他的話語不再只是哲學，而是有了真實的重量。
1) lived through it (phr.): 親身經歷並存活；syn: survived; ant: avoided
2) intellectual concept (n.): 抽象的概念；syn: theoretical idea; ant: lived experience
pronunciation: Credibility: HAV-ing LIVED through it | a BIT more CER-tain-ty | pure-ly in-tel-LEC-tu-al CON-cept.

example: He states the universal truth that no person truly wishes for death.
hint:
中文解釋：看似簡單的陳述，卻是引出後面深刻討論的起點——死亡是每個人都無法迴避的終點。
1) no one (pron.): 沒有人；syn: nobody; ant: everyone
2) wants to die (phr.): 想要死去；syn: desires death; ant: wants to live
pronunciation: Universal: NO one | WANTS to DIE. (quiet, matter-of-fact)

word: Even people who want to go to heaven don't want to die to get there.
meaning: 即使是那些想上天堂的人，也不想死著去那裡。
example: He humorously notes that even those who believe in heaven still fear or avoid death.
hint:
中文解釋：帶著幽默的觀察，點出人對死亡的矛盾——嚮往天堂，卻不願死亡。
1) go to heaven (phr.): 上天堂；syn: reach the afterlife; ant: stay in this world
2) to get there (phr.): 為了到達那裡；syn: in order to arrive; ant: (n/a)
pronunciation: Wry: E-ven people who WANT to go to HEA-ven | don't WANT to DIE | to GET there.

word: And yet, death is the destination we all share.
meaning: 然而，死亡是我們所有人共同的終點。
example: Despite our reluctance, death is the one inevitable destination for every person.
hint:
中文解釋：帶著肅穆感的普世真理——死亡沒有例外，是所有人共同的命運。
1) destination (n.): 目的地、終點；syn: final stop; ant: starting point
2) we all share (phr.): 我們所有人共有的；syn: universal; ant: unique to some
pronunciation: Solemn: and YET | DEATH is the des-TI-na-tion | we ALL share.

word: No one has ever escaped it.
meaning: 從來沒有人能夠逃脫它。
example: Throughout all of human history, no one has ever avoided death.
hint:
中文解釋：簡短有力的歷史聲明——從古至今，沒有例外，這是最終的平等。
1) escaped (v.): 逃脫；syn: avoided; ant: faced
2) ever (adv.): 曾經、從來；syn: at any time; ant: never
pronunciation: Final: NO one | has EV-er es-CAPED it. (firm, no room for doubt)
